Despite facing a second trade secrets lawsuit involving its hardware business in just over a year, OpenAI is still planning to launch its first product this year and begin commercial rollout in 2027, according to Bloomberg. Details below.

The first product launch timeline remains unchanged at 2026.

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device plans.

The complaint details the methods by which the former OpenAI employees allegedly stole Apple's trade secrets on multiple occasions, and alleges that 'this type of misconduct has become routine and is led by example from the company's leadership.'

Following the earlier lawsuit filed by startup iyO, the new lawsuit further deepens the legal troubles surrounding OpenAI's hardware business. That case initially focused on a branding dispute, but the complaint was later amended to include allegations of trade secret theft.

Despite news of the lawsuit breaking last Friday, OpenAI appears to be sticking to its original hardware timeline. According to Bloomberg:

Since announcing the partnership with io Products, Jony Ive's company, to develop an 'AI-first' device, speculation has swirled about exactly what OpenAI has in mind.

After the partnership was announced in May 2025, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo immediately pointed out that OpenAI's first device would be a small, screenless wearable designed to be worn around the neck, equipped with cameras and microphones to capture the user's surroundings, with computing and display functions handled by a smartphone.

On the other hand, OpenAI has also hinted that it plans to release multiple devices rather than just one product, and stated in legal filings related to the iyO lawsuit that the first product would not be an in-ear or wearable form factor as speculated when the partnership was announced.
